external_assessment.report:
Overall: partial. Candidate: partial. Verifier: partial; its unqualified accepted disposition is not justified by its reproduced evidence.

The candidate substantially meets both requested criteria and the requested shape: one short summary, two findings, and at most one citation per finding. Its diagnosis finding is supported by its valid, though broad, citation to the supplied test lines 1–52. Specifically, lines 19–22 establish the answer and response message before the injected failure, line 28 confirms the observed reply, and lines 45–52 identify one failed agent turn for this run and reject the three case-folded substrings. Its stated limitation—that other diagnostic phrasing and the exact full message are not checked—is concrete and supported by those assertions. It does not infer the historical SDK exception cause.

The settlement finding has a valid citation address but insufficient citation support. Supplied new-message.txt:1 contains only “The summoning faltered. This request could not be completed.” It supports the description of the replacement text as generic, but none of the FAILED, SETTLED, error, or DONE assertions. Those claims instead have support in the supplied test: line 33 is `assert run.status is RunStatus.FAILED`, line 34 is `assert run.error == str(failure)`, line 36 is `assert delivery.state is RunDeliveryState.SETTLED`, and line 37 requires exactly one FAILED DONE payload. The candidate’s wording “run.error equals the RuntimeError” also blurs the asserted string value with the exception object: exception identity is separately checked for caught.value at line 29. This is a precision defect, not a missing settlement check.

The verifier correctly preserves the supported diagnosis finding and the useful limitation, but simply repeats the settlement claim with the same unrelated citation and error-value imprecision. Its empty contradictions list does not establish that the cited source entails the claim. Acceptance therefore overstates what its reasoning has validated.

Practical utility: the answer is useful as a compact guide to the supplied regression’s asserted behavior, with the above evidence and precision limits. The text shows a synthetic RuntimeError raised after a model reply (lines 14, 19–22), not a reproduced historical SDK failure. The assertions cover this failed turn’s three substrings, not every possible capability diagnosis or emission channel; helper bodies and the full worker are expressly omitted. No passing execution or broader implementation behavior can be established from this packet alone.
